headline: S&P -4.4% Thursday, VIX 28, 2y 4.46%, Brent $97, Nikkei -6%, chips +3-10% pre-mkt, NFP 8:30
stance: Thursday was a full-book unwind on a policy headline; the bounce starts in chips. Payrolls 8:30 decides whether the 2y rally holds: consensus +59-65K, 4.2%.

news.head: Chips bounce pre-market after SOX -12.2% Thursday
news.body: Lam +9.8%, Micron +7.4%, AMD +6.6%, Nvidia +3.4% (~5am ET). Thursday: AMD -17.3%, Micron -17.5%, Nvidia -9.3%, SanDisk -22%. SOX worst since March 2020.

news.head: CoreWeave 5y CDS record 1,268bp, stock -10% Thursday
news.body: SpaceX 5y CDS record 284bp; ING is selling a ~$500mn data-center loan book. Hyperscaler CDS cheaper since the election. Neoclouds pay, not Big Tech.

news.head: Airbnb: Q3 revenue $4.9bn, +19%, new $12bn buyback
news.body: GBV $27.7bn, +21%; nights +16%; adj. EBITDA $2.5bn, 52% margin. Q4 revenue guide $3.22-3.28bn, +16-18%. FY growth raised to high teens.

news.head: Microchip -3.5% after hours on a light Q3 guide
news.body: Q2 EPS $0.97 vs $0.93, revenue $1.622bn vs $1.607bn; Q3 guide midpoint below consensus. Charter, Humana, Moderna and Under Armour report before the open.

implications: Permitting is the new AI risk: ~30% of 2028 US data-center additions exposed to construction pauses. Debt-funded developers eat it; owners of built capacity hold the scarce asset.
A 2y at 4.46% against a 70% December hike is the mismatch. A payrolls print above 80K is the test for the 5y longs, 99th %ile, that Thursday just paid.

watch.head: Payrolls 8:30: +59-65K consensus, 4.2% unemployment
watch.body: AHE +0.3% expected vs +0.1%. Claims 189K Thursday, matching a 57-year low; ADP +86K. A print at or below 30K takes out the ~20% January hike pricing.

watch.head: UMich prelim 10:00; consumer credit 3:00
watch.body: First household inflation-expectations read since Brent fell 12% on the week. Canada jobs 8:30: +13.6K consensus, 6.5% unemployment.

watch.head: Hormuz: IRGC says two tankers struck mines Friday
watch.body: Five more claimed Thursday, none confirmed by maritime officials. Attacks near a record pace. Iran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar.

watch.head: CPI Tuesday Nov 10, 8:30
watch.body: First inflation print under a 70% December hike. The 1y US inflation swap hit a 2-month low of 2.16% Thursday; euro 1y swap 3.10%. PPI follows Friday.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Dec 9 hike odds ~70% (~9pm ET Thursday), from 80%+ Wednesday. The 2y did the work: lowest since early September. Two Fed speakers backed gradual hikes.
Brent $96.93, -1.4% (~4:40am ET) after +5% Thursday and a run at $100 overnight; week -12%. Tanker attacks put the floor under it, not OPEC.
DXY 101.80 (~midnight ET), off Thursday's low since late September. EUR/USD 1.118 (~2:30am ET) from a 1.127 Thursday high. Haven bid, not a rates bid.
sections.positioning: Specs long 5y, 99th %ile, 8 weeks (background): Thursday paid them. New this week: platinum specs to the 14th %ile, -21 pts w/w, an extended short.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P futures +0.4%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.9%, Dow futures -0.9% (~2-4am ET). Thursday: tech sector -7.3%, industrials -4.1%; Nasdaq -11.9% from the Oct 6 record.
Nikkei -6.0% Friday, below 60,000, worst since April 2025. Kospi -6.0% after an 8.8% intraday halt; week -12%. Stoxx 600 -1.6% at the open (~3:10am ET).
~$47bn of leveraged-ETF rebalance selling hit Thursday's close, second largest since 2006. Spot VIX closed above 3-month: hedges bought, not rolled.
sections.positioning: Specs long Nasdaq 100 96th %ile and Russell 2000 99th %ile for 5-6 weeks (background): Thursday hit full books. VIX shorts 13th %ile, +9 pts w/w.

single_name.note: New to the screen Nov 4, score 5: insider rule fired, above its 200-day line, 4.6 days to cover. A regional bank on the day the AI book sold.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Asian IG dollar spreads 73bp Thursday, widest since July 2025. US and Asian credit selling stayed measured; lower Treasury yields cushioned total returns.
Hedge funds have been net sellers of AI-financing debt for weeks. Tech issued ~$500bn of debt this year, 9 IG deals of $25bn+. Supply is the spread risk.
Barkin Friday: $500bn+ of AI debt financing this year is a credit risk, concentrated in financial intermediaries. The permitting shock lands on that debt first.
sections.positioning: No credit COT extreme. Dealer IG inventory 21st %ile of 3 years, unchanged: balance sheet to warehouse AI supply when issuance reopens.
